correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-variable antiderivative tests yield \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=x\), \(\mathbb E[xz\mid y]=cy\), and \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=bz\). Their integrated and weighted forms give \(\mathbb E[x^2]=b\mathbb E[z]\), \(c\mathbb E[y^2]=b\mathbb E[z^2]\), and exactly \(\mathbb E[z(z-c)]=(c/b)\mathbb E[(y-x)^2]\). Zero defect forces the invariant support into \(y=x\); tangency and bounded completeness reduce that support to the origin and the two nonzero equilibria. The packaged checker verifies the generator and defect algebra exactly.

value.rationale: The Lü system is a canonical bridge between Lorenz and Chen dynamics, and its two nonzero equilibria share the natural height \(z=c\) while the origin sits at \(z=0\). The theorem turns those equilibrium heights into a global stationary obstruction: every genuinely non-equilibrium compact recurrent state must place positive mass outside the entire equilibrium-height slab. The three exact conditional laws are finer than ordinary time averages and give binwise identities that can be checked on periodic or chaotic invariant data. The square-defect equality classification distinguishes equilibrium mixing sharply from recurrent dynamics, making the result a structural invariant-measure constraint rather than a numerical re-estimation of known chaos diagnostics.
